# The tests each CI job may skip, and why (.github/scripts/skips.py reads it).
# A test that cannot run on a machine returns early and prints why
# ("skipped: ..."); a job fails on a skip this list does not give it, so a
# runner that loses Landlock, user namespaces or its systemd user session
# fails instead of passing with less tested. A name here that did not skip
# is only noted. One line per test: <job> <test name as cargo prints it> <why>.
#
# Jobs: linux (ci.yml, the runner's account), linux-root (the same runner,
# the tests that need root run as root), linux-userns (the same runner and
# account with user namespaces open: tests/own_proc.rs), windows (ci.yml).
# The other jobs run their tests one by one and fail on their own.

# Root, or root of a user namespace that may change owners and mount: the
# runner's account is neither, and ubuntu-24.04 restricts user namespaces
# with AppArmor. They run in the linux-root step.
linux acl::tests::remove_all_gives_what_nerve_run_made_to_the_owner needs root; runs as root in the next step
linux acl::tests::remove_all_gives_no_file_with_a_second_name needs a mount namespace; runs as root in the next step
linux acl::tests::a_revoked_inner_grant_on_another_file_system_stays_stale needs a mount namespace; runs as root in the next step
linux acl::tests::a_revoked_inner_grant_the_owner_cannot_reach_stays_stale needs a mount namespace; runs as root in the next step
linux the_backup_file_is_opened_as_the_user_who_asked needs root or a user namespace; runs as root in the next step
linux root_starts_in_a_folder_only_its_owner_may_enter needs root or a user namespace; runs as root in the next step
linux a_root_node_keeps_its_rights_over_other_accounts_files needs root; runs as root in the next step
linux-userns a_root_node_keeps_its_rights_over_other_accounts_files needs root; runs as root in the step before

# A command's own /proc: the shim makes a user namespace as the runner's
# account, which ubuntu-24.04's AppArmor holds back from it
# (apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns). Root makes none, so they cannot
# run as root either. They run in the linux-userns step, with the
# restriction lifted.
linux a_command_in_its_own_namespace_ends_as_it_would_without needs a user namespace, which AppArmor holds back; runs in the linux-userns step
linux a_capability_a_center_added_has_a_proc_of_its_own needs a user namespace, which AppArmor holds back; runs in the linux-userns step
linux a_command_of_one_pairing_does_not_see_a_running_command_of_another needs a user namespace, which AppArmor holds back; runs in the linux-userns step
linux the_cgroup_has_room_for_the_shim_and_the_init needs a user namespace, which AppArmor holds back; runs in the linux-userns step

# Landlock ABI 9 (Linux 7.1), which keeps unix sockets by path to the
# pairing's folders while the network switch is off: the runner's kernel has
# 7.0 (ABI 8). It runs on a kernel with ABI 9.
linux a_folder_command_without_network_reaches_unix_sockets_in_its_folders_only needs Landlock ABI 9 (Linux 7.1); the runner has ABI 8
